questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design multi-tenant SSH access using Vault's dynamic secrets, ensuring tenant isolation, short lifetimes, auditability, and rapid rollback during tenant disablement.

## Key Concepts
- SSH secret engine, dynamic certs, per-tenant roles, TTLs, and CA management
- Lease-based revocation for rapid tenant disablement
- Audit trails and scoped access controls

## Code Example
```bash
# Enable SSH engine
vault secrets enable -path=ssh ssh

# Create tenant role
vault write ssh/roles/tenant-<id>-dev allowed_users="tenant-<id>-dev" ip_blacklist="" ttl=15m

# Request sign (CSR flow varies by client; concept shown)
vault sign ssh/tenant-<id>-dev -field=certificate <csr.pem
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor and verify revocation and prevent certificate reuse?
- How would you scale this design to thousands of tenants and multiple bastions?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests KV v2 versioning, per-tenant isolation via policies, and practical onboarding steps with Vault CLI.

## Key Concepts
- KV v2 path scoping
- Policy creation and binding
- AppRole or token auth
- Rollback and isolation testing

## Code Example
```bash
vault secrets enable -path=tenant-<id> kv-v2
vault policy write tenant-admin-<id> - <<'EOF'
path "tenant-<id>/*" {
  capabilities = ["create","read","update","delete","list"]
}
EOF
vault policy write tenant-app-<id> - <<'EOF'
path "tenant-<id>/*" {
  capabilities = ["read","list"]
}
EOF
```

```bash
vault write auth/approle/role/tenant-app-<id> token_ttl=30m policies=tenant-app-<id>
vault kv put tenant-<id>/config/feature enabled=true
```


```bash
# Rollback
vault token revoke <token>
vault delete auth/approle/role/tenant-app-<id>
vault delete policy/tenant-admin-<id>
vault erase kv/tenant-<id>
```

```bash
# Namespace setup (per tenant)
vault namespace create ns-tenantA

path "ssh/tenantA/*" { capabilities = ["read", "list"] }
```
